DisabledTests.SkipEarlyData-SecondClientHelloEarlyData: KEEP: the second ClientHello keeps its `early_data` extension, which §4.1.2's exception list forbids — "removing the early_data extension ... if one was present. Early data is not permitted after a HelloRetryRequest." We refuse that hello with illegal_parameter; BoringSSL accepts it and lets the early-data record behind it fail to decrypt, so the case wants bad_record_mac. Both end the connection and ours ends it one message earlier, on the rule that was actually broken — the same §4.1.2 list we enforce for `pre_shared_key`, where BoGo demanded it (`Resume-Server-OmitAllPSKsOnSecondClientHello`). docs/BOGO.md finding 14.

DisabledTests.TLS13-DuplicateTicketEarlyDataSupport: KEEP: a NewSessionTicket carrying `early_data` twice. We refuse it with the error the case asks for (`zssl:DuplicateExtension`) and differ only in the alert: ours is decode_error, BoringSSL's is illegal_parameter. §4.2 states one rule for "a given extension block" and names no alert, and zssl enforces it with one pre-pass over every block it reads — so it is one error, and an error is all the library returns. Two alerts for one rule would mean two error names for one rule. BoringSSL's split follows its own code structure rather than §6.2, and its corpus asks both ways: decode_error for `DuplicateExtensionClient/Server-TLS-TLS13`, illegal_parameter here. docs/BOGO.md finding 15.
